note: Triennial election of Down County Council, polled Thursday 2 June 1955 (Belfast Telegraph, 1 June 1955: 'POLLING DAY - To-morrow 2nd JUNE'). Saintfield was the only contested division: the retiring member, Lieut.-Col. Perceval Price (Unionist), polled 1,543 against 843 for Mr. James Lilley, also Unionist. The other nineteen divisions were filled unopposed. The Returning Officer's notice of result (Belfast Telegraph, 4 June 1955) lists all twenty divisions and the candidate returned for each; it prints no party labels. The official notice prints the surname as Percival-Price in the candidates' column and Perceval-Price in the elected column; the news report prints 'Perceval Price' and 'Mr. James Lillie'. Price was the retiring member.
